note: current = measured live on this machine. latest = each vendor's newest public release, checked daily from its release feed (version_check.py); the values here are the fallback when that check is off or offline. An installed build newer than any public release is shown as its own target. Driver/BIOS staleness is judged by age. perf = estimated performance/stability benefit (0-100).

catalog.name: WSL 2 platform
catalog.why: WSL updates carry autoMemoryReclaim + networking-mode improvements that directly reduce the vmmemWSL footprint. Update with `wsl --update`.

catalog.name: WSL 2 kernel
catalog.why: The WSL2 Linux kernel governs guest memory reclaim and virtio I/O. Ships with `wsl --update`.

catalog.name: Wi-Fi / network driver
catalog.channel: Windows Update (optional updates) / PC maker's support app
catalog.why: A current network driver improves sustained throughput, roaming stability and power, and fixes latency spikes.

catalog.name: Graphics driver
catalog.channel: Windows Update (optional updates) / GPU or PC maker's support app
catalog.why: Newer graphics drivers fix rendering stalls and improve compositor and WebView2 performance.

catalog.name: Node.js runtime
catalog.why: Node 22 LTS ships a newer V8 with faster startup, JIT and GC. This is a MAJOR bump requiring a NodeSource channel switch and a re-test of global tooling (ExcelJS etc.) - apply deliberately, not blindly. Node 20 is patched to 20.20.2 in-channel.

catalog.name: PowerShell
catalog.why: PowerShell 7.6.6 installed alongside the frozen Windows PowerShell 5.1 (user-scope portable, no admin needed) - faster startup/parsing. For a machine-wide managed install, IT can run `winget install Microsoft.PowerShell` elevated. The collector still uses 5.1 for compatibility.

catalog.name: Microsoft Edge
catalog.why: Edge + WebView2 dominate process/handle counts here. It auto-updates, so it is usually at most a few days behind; trimming extensions and idle tabs helps more than the version.

catalog.name: WebView2 Runtime
catalog.why: WebView2 backs many app UIs (Teams, Outlook, GlobalProtect). The evergreen runtime keeps itself current.

catalog.name: Ubuntu (WSL distro)
catalog.why: Ubuntu 26.04 LTS is available as a release upgrade (LTS to LTS). Until then keep 24.04 patched with `sudo apt update && sudo apt full-upgrade`.

catalog.name: UEFI / BIOS firmware
catalog.why: UEFI/BIOS updates improve power/thermal management, Thunderbolt/Wi-Fi stability and ship Intel microcode and security fixes.

catalog.name: Kiro CLI
catalog.why: Keep current via the built-in updater; newer builds add faster tool routing and lower memory use.

catalog.name: nginx web server
catalog.why: At the LTS-maintained version (security-backported). The upstream 1.28 stable branch (HTTP/3/QUIC) needs the nginx.org repo and an nginx restart that briefly drops the dashboard + 3PP API - a deliberate change, not auto-applied.

catalog.name: Docker engine
catalog.why: Current; keep patched for containerd/runc performance and CVE fixes.

catalog.name: Python 3 runtime
catalog.why: At the LTS-maintained version (security-backported; the interpreter that runs this dashboard and the API). Upstream 3.12.7 would need deadsnakes/source and risks the system Python - do NOT auto-replace.

catalog.name: gunicorn (API server)
catalog.why: Serves the 3PP dashboard API; current.

catalog.name: Windows 11 build
catalog.why: IT-managed; newer builds carry scheduler, memory-compression and security-agent interoperability fixes.

catalog.name: Git
catalog.why: At the LTS-maintained version. Upstream 2.46 (faster large-repo status/checkout) needs the git-core PPA.

catalog.name: Python (runs SysPerf)
catalog.channel: Microsoft Store auto-update or python.org installer
catalog.why: The interpreter the dashboard, collector and agent run on. Patch releases inside the same 3.11 line are safe; a new minor line needs the venv rebuilt (re-run install.ps1).

catalog.name: Flask (web framework)
catalog.why: Serves the dashboard API. Pinned so every install behaves the same; change the pin deliberately and run the quality gates.

catalog.name: waitress (web server)
catalog.why: The production WSGI server SysPerf runs under on 127.0.0.1. Without it SysPerf falls back to Flask's development server.

catalog.name: pytest (test runner)
catalog.why: Runs the 1,000+ test suite behind the unit and coverage gates (the Auto-Improve tab's self-test). Not needed to run the dashboard itself.

catalog.name: Playwright (browser testing)
catalog.channel: pip install playwright, then: playwright install chromium
catalog.why: Drives a real browser for the 'browser' quality gate (100% UI coverage). Without it that gate is skipped on this machine; the dashboard itself does not need it.

catalog.name: Chromium for Playwright
catalog.why: The headless browser the browser gate runs. Installed per user under ms-playwright; reinstall after upgrading Playwright.

catalog.name: Git for Windows
catalog.why: Self-evolution keeps every AI patch in git worktrees and review branches, and Apply/Roll back are git operations.

catalog.name: Claude Code (AI provider)
catalog.why: The model provider that proposes self-evolution patches, run headless with all tools disabled.

catalog.name: bubblewrap (evolution sandbox)
catalog.why: Runs AI-written code with no network and a read-only filesystem. Without it every evolution cycle stops as 'blocked'.

catalog.name: npm
catalog.why: Managed by the nodejs package; moves with Node upgrades rather than being self-updated on a distro install.
